title: Strict right-fibration slices compared naturally with intrinsic slices
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the infinity category $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ and its coherent classification conventions of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening], and strict right fibrations of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. For a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $D$, let $\mathsf R(D)$ be the simplicial category of $\mathcal U$-small strict right fibrations $E\to D$, with mapping Kan complex $\operatorname{Fun}_{/D}(E,E')$ of strict maps $E\times\Delta^n\to E'$ over $D$. Let $R_{\mathrm{int}}(D)$ be the full subcategory of the infinity-categorical slice $(\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U})_{/D}$ on arrows equivalent in that slice to strict right fibrations. Its arrows include the specified triangle homotopies. Sending a strict right fibration and its strict maps to the corresponding slice objects and maps induces an equivalence
$$N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathsf R(D)\simeq R_{\mathrm{int}}(D).$$
Here $N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ is the homotopy coherent nerve of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. In particular the comparison identifies the strict mapping Kan complex with the mapping space in the infinity slice. Strict pullback along $h:D\to D'$ corresponds under this equivalence to infinity-categorical base change along $h$. The strict-pullback assignment $D\mapsto N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathsf R(D)$ descends through categorical equivalences of base quasicategories, and these comparisons form a natural equivalence of functors $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U'}$. This includes arbitrary coherent transformations and all higher base simplices, not just strictly composable base maps. All slice and functor categories are formed in containing universes.

source.place: Chu--Haugseng Proposition 6.2, proof final paragraph (strict relative-category comparison); GHN Appendix A, Proposition A.30, Corollary A.32 and the right-fibration variant explicitly used there; Hinich, arXiv:1311.4128v4, Proposition 2.1.4 and its cartesian dual. This is only the strict/intrinsic slice comparison, not the classification by presheaves. Online sources read; archives WANTED. No Stacks tag.

proof.text: The section-mapping theorem [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent-gluing] makes $\mathsf R(D)$ locally Kan. Regard a quasicategory $A$ as an object of the locally Kan simplicial category with mapping complexes $\operatorname{Fun}(A,B)^\simeq$; its nerve is $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ by [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. A simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}_{/D}(E,E')$ lies in this core: each edge in its parameter direction evaluates at $e\in E$ to an edge of the Kan fiber $E'_{p(e)}$, hence an equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-core-kan-fibration]; the pointwise criterion then applies. Thus forgetting the base is an enriched functor, equipped with the strictly enriched natural transformation to the constant object $D$ whose component is $p:E\to D$. Concretely this is an enriched functor $\mathsf R(D)\times[1]\to\mathsf Q$, sending a cross-interval map to $p$; enriched naturality is precisely $p'f=p$. The coherent nerve preserves this product (a functor into a product is a pair of functors). It supplies a coherent transformation to the constant diagram $D$, hence a functor $J_D$ to the arrow-model slice of $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$. The slice-arrow equivalence identifies this with the intrinsic slice. On vertices and strict arrows it is the comparison in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 6.2, strict-arrow relative model; enriched comparison and its maps written explicitly

proof.text:
A right fibration between quasicategories is an isofibration. Indeed take opposites, apply [lem-cbc-left-fibration-equivalence-lift], and take opposites back; [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4) preserves equivalences and isofibrations. The equivalence lift with prescribed target in the left-fibration statement supplies precisely the prescribed-source lift on the right-fibration side. Therefore exponentiation of $p':E'\to D$ by $E$, followed by passage to cores, is a Kan fibration
$$\operatorname{Fun}(E,E')^\simeq\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(E,D)^\simeq.$$
Its strict fiber over $p$ is exactly $\operatorname{Fun}_{/D}(E,E')$: the previous step checked that every relative simplex lies in the core. By [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] insertion of the constant path identifies this strict fiber with the homotopy fiber over $p$.

source.place: Isofibration exponential and core mapping-space test; right-fibration dual of equivalence lifting

proof.text: Apply the cone-category mapping formula [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] in $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ with indexing shape $\Delta^0$ and target $D$. The mapping space from $p:E\to D$ to $p':E'\to D$ is the homotopy fiber over $p$ of postcomposition by $p'$ on $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Cat}}(E,E')$. The marked-point model identifies these two mapping spaces with the cores in step 2. The constant-path comparison there is induced by $J_D$, since $p'f=p$ is its specified triangle. The coherent-nerve mapping comparison identifies the source mapping space with $\operatorname{Fun}_{/D}(E,E')$, respecting composition. Thus $J_D$ is fully faithful. Its essential image is exactly $R_{\mathrm{int}}(D)$ by that subcategory's definition. The full-essential-image theorem gives the asserted equivalence and the mapping-space identification, without using presheaf classification.

source.place: Proposition 6.2, identification of the strict relative model with the intrinsic right-fibration fiber

proof.text: For $h:D\to D'$ and $p':E'\to D'$, degreewise pullback $D\times_{D'}E'\to D$ is a right fibration: compose a horn lifting problem with the projection to $E'$ and use its right-fibration filler, retaining the specified map to $D$. The total space is a quasicategory, since the same argument fills inner horns over the corresponding filler in $D$. Step 2 makes $p'$ an isofibration, so [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] identifies the displayed strict square with its infinity-categorical pullback. The construction on a relative $n$-simplex is $(d,e,t)\mapsto(d,f(e,t))$; it commutes with every simplex operator and composition. Consequently it gives the family of limiting squares on the entire enriched category $\mathsf R(D')$, identifying strict pullback with intrinsic base change under $J$. Pullback along an equivalence is an equivalence on intrinsic slices: compose with pullback along an inverse, and use the two inverse equivalences and the pullback universal property to identify the composites with the identity. It restricts to the full right-fibration images. With step 3 this proves that $h^*$ is an equivalence whenever $h$ is a categorical equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 6.2, pullback stability and intrinsic cartesian transport; strict pullbacks compute the specified cones

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B$ be the ordinary category of $\mathcal U$-small quasicategories and simplicial maps, with $U$ the categorical equivalences. Its coherent localization is $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$. To verify this with the actual base map, equip every quasicategory with its equivalence marking. Every simplicial functor preserves these markings, so $\mathcal B$ identifies with the ordinary fibrant subcategory of the marked-point model. All objects there are cofibrant; [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identifies its ordinary localization with the coherent nerve of its fibrant simplicial category, and [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model] identifies that nerve and its vertex map with $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ and the usual inclusion. Work in a containing universe, since the collection of $\mathcal U$-small objects is not itself $\mathcal U$-small. On fibrant objects the marked weak-equivalence test is the core mapping test. Taking its target successively to be the source and target of a tested map gives an inverse and the two inverse homotopies; conversely such an inverse makes every core mapping test an equivalence. Thus its weak equivalences agree with $U$.

source.place: Section 1.3, especially Propositions 1.3.4--1.3.5, applied to the marked-point model

proof.text:
For each $D\in\mathcal B$, give the ordinary category $\mathcal E_D$ of strict right fibrations over $D$ the weak equivalences $W_D$ detected by categorical equivalence of total quasicategories. These are exactly the fiberwise weak homotopy equivalences: one direction is [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers], and the converse follows from the inverse over $D$ supplied by [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent-gluing]. That inverse is a coherent quasi-inverse of total spaces; its simplicial homotopies are pointwise equivalences because the fibers are Kan. These are also precisely the contravariant model weak equivalences between fibrant objects by [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation]. That model has every object cofibrant and enrichment $\operatorname{Fun}_{/D}$, so the simplicial model localization theorem gives a canonical equivalence
$$L(\mathcal E_D,W_D)\simeq N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathsf R(D).$$
It agrees with the vertex inclusion and enriched mapping spaces. Pullback preserves $W_D$, since it preserves the inverse and both relative homotopies (or simply uses the displayed fiberwise criterion). By step 4 it induces equivalences of these localizations for all $h\in U$.

source.place: Proposition 6.2, relative categories of fibrant objects; GHN Appendix A, right-fibration variant

proof.text: Form the ordinary total category $\mathcal E$: objects are strict right fibrations $E\to D$ with $D\in\mathcal B$, and arrows are strictly commuting squares $(f,h)$. Projection to $D$ is a Grothendieck fibration. Its cartesian lift over $h:D\to D'$ with target $E'\to D'$ is the degreewise pullback square: a square over $hk$ factors uniquely by the pair of its top map and its map to $D$. Chosen iterated pullbacks have canonical associators given by reassociating tuples; both composites in the associativity condition send a tuple to the same tuple. Steps 4 and 6 verify all hypotheses of [lem-coef-relative-grothendieck-localization] with $U$ and $W_D$ above. Thus $L\mathcal E\to L\mathcal B$ is an intrinsic cartesian family with fiber $N_{\mathrm{hc}}\mathsf R(D)$, and with transport the localization of strict pullback. In particular this is the descent of the strict-pullback assignment, with its coherent family structure.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.4 and proof 2.2.2--2.2.6, cartesian dual; GHN Proposition A.30

proof.text: The intrinsic comparison family is the full subcategory $\mathcal T\subseteq\operatorname{Arr}(\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U})$ on arrows equivalent to strict right fibrations. The category $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}$ has pullbacks by [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure]. By [lem-coef-arrow-target-cartesian-pullbacks], target evaluation on the whole arrow category is cartesian. Its lifts stay in $\mathcal T$ by step 4 and invariance under equivalence, so its restriction is cartesian as well: the mapping-space universal property of such a lift is unchanged on restricting the test objects to a full subcategory. Its fiber is $R_{\mathrm{int}}(D)$. Send a strict square in $\mathcal E$ to the corresponding coherent square in $\mathcal T$, using the base localization map of step 5. This is a coherent functor on $N\mathcal E$, not a choice of separate comparison functors.

source.place: Proposition 6.2, first paragraph and final paragraph: full right-fibration arrow category

proof.text: For a marked arrow of $\mathcal E$ in step 7, its base map $h$ is in $U$, and its vertical factor is in $W_D$. The cartesian factor is an infinity-categorical pullback along an equivalence by step 4, hence also an equivalence on total objects. Thus both components of the resulting square are equivalences. The pointwise equivalence criterion in the arrow functor category makes this an equivalence in $\mathcal T$. The entire-functor-category universal property of localization therefore factors the preceding coherent functor through $L\mathcal E$. It preserves cartesian edges: images of ordinary cartesian lifts are the limiting squares of step 4, and [lem-coef-relative-grothendieck-localization] says these suffice. Its functor on each fiber is $J_D$ under step 6. Indeed both comparisons arise from the same strict structure arrows and strict commuting triangles; localization identifies their extensions including transformations. Apply Cartesian straightening (the opposite form of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]) to this map of cartesian families. It gives a coherent natural transformation between their classifying functors on $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal U}^{\mathrm{op}}$. Its components are the equivalences of step 3, so the pointwise equivalence criterion makes it a natural equivalence. This constructs the comparison on every coherent base simplex, with all face and degeneracy compatibilities inherited from the map of families. It also identifies its transport along $h$ with the strict pullback already calculated, as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NZ-ee5ff3249 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, all nine steps and the full statement of every cited node. I read both sources at the cited places, fetched into /tmp: Chu–Haugseng 2006.08269 Prop 6.2 and its final paragraph (pp. 12–13), and Hinich 1311.4128v4 Def 2.1.1, Prop 2.1.4 and proof 2.2.2–2.2.6 (pp. 17–21). The item statement is unchanged from the base and is not weakened. Small cases D=∅ and D=Δ⁰ hold, and empty fibers are allowed. Steps 1–9 each check against the cited statements: core containment of Fun_{/D} via the Kan fibers; prescribed-source lifts through the opposite left-fibration lift; strict fiber ≃ homotopy fiber through the path comparison; full faithfulness and the essential image; strict pullback ≃ ∞-pullback (isofibration-pullback-limit); L(sSet-qcat, equivalences) ≃ Cat∞ (marked-point model plus model localization); W_D equal to the fiberwise and contravariant weak equivalences; the new lemma's hypotheses; RFib inheriting cartesian edges (CH first paragraph); the map of families, then straightening and the pointwise criterion. In step 6, L(h*) being an equivalence follows from step 4's natural limiting squares plus the localization universal property. The new node lem-coef-relative-grothendieck-localization is the cartesian dual of Hinich 2.1.4: its V is Remark 2.1.2's generated marking, and the preserved cartesian lifts and the classifying functor come from 2.2.2. It is not a duplicate. lem-coef-grothendieck-fibre-localization needs model-category fibers with all-weak-equivalence-preserving transitions over a fixed base, which fails here: {1}⊂Δ¹ is right anodyne, but its fiber over 0 is ∅→Δ⁰. lem-coef-localization-cartesian-pullback gives only the base-localization half. The report missed both candidates. There is no cycle, and I accept both declared tool_uses (cbc cone calculus and left-fibration equivalence lift). One fix (B3): the new node used Cat∞ and 'classifying coherent functor' without citing a node. I added lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening to its stmt_deps and statement in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-coef-relative-grothendieck-localization.json.
